newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chilean leader visits Paris to sign eight accords.
newsitem.headline: Chilean leader visits Paris to sign eight accords.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei began a four-day state visit to France on Wednesday to capitalise on a strengthening of ties between Paris and the countries of South America's Mercosur economic powerhouse.

Frei's trip came two weeks after French President Jacques Chirac toured the four Mercosur countries -- Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay -- and Bolivia which like Chile is an associate of the fast-growing trade group.

"I believe that...Chirac's initiative to seek a deepening of ties between the European Union and Chile, Mercosur and Latin America has a tremendous potential," Frei, who earlier visited Brussels, told Radio France Internationale.
He told reporters after meeting Prime Minister Alain Juppe that they discussed the eight cooperation accords to be signed during his visit, the main one concerning education and culture.

Frei is the last of the heads of state of South America's southern cone to visit France. Chirac has blamed this on schedule problems, denying that it was due to Chile's protests against French nuclear tests in the South Pacific.
The 1995-1996 tests halted a rapprochement which had started with the return of democracy in Chile in 1990 after 17 years of icy relations with the dictatorship of General Augusto Pinochet.

Frei told the daily Le Figaro that Chirac's tour and his own visit heralded "a new vision of ties between France, a great pillar of development, and a Latin America engaged in strengthening democracy."
He backed Chirac's call, made during his South American tour, for a summit between Latin America and Europe and hoped the initiative would soon crystalise into a definite proposal.

In South America, Chirac emphasised the potential for boosting exchanges with France and with the European Union, which signed a trade agreement with Mercosur two years ago and has already become its main trade partner.
French diplomats said Frei's visit would encourage French business to invest in Chile, one of Latin America's fastest-growing economies.

France is now the 10th largest investor in Chile, with French companies holding interests in public works, banking, telecommunications, insurance and wineries. The construction group Spie-Batignolles owns Chile's top ski resort, Valle Nevado.

Trade between the two countries was worth $950 million last year when Chile recorded a trade deficit with France for the first time this decade. Frei was expected to ask Chirac to ease trade barriers for Chilean exports, which Santiago blames for the deficit.
Frei's visit will also revive old cultural affinities which prompted many Chileans to seek asylum in France after Pinochet's 1973 coup.

A seven-tonne, five-metre (17-foot) tall replica of a "Moai" -- the long-faced statues of Chile's Easter Island -- is to go on show at Paris' Trocadero gardens, and the Louvre museum will stage an exhibit on the late popular Chilean poet and folk singer Violeta Para.
